intro: An AI agent wrote this page from saved copies of its sources. Separate AI checkers, which never saw the drafting, then checked it in rounds. In this trial, no person checked the facts. Here is what the checkers did, what they found, and what is still open.

sections.title: What we checked
paras: Each round runs the same checks. A page passes a round only when every check passes. After that, we fix only sentences that misstate a source or break our writing rules, and a fresh checker looks again at just those sentences. Other suggestions wait for the next full round.
head: Check
What it does
Pass mark
rows: Code confirms that every sentence cites a source passage or is labeled as our analysis, that quotes match word for word, that saved files match their fingerprints, and that the reading level is about grade 8 or lower.
A separate AI checker sees only this page and the source passages. For each sentence it must copy the exact words that support it, and code confirms those words are really there.

Three more AI checkers. One speaks up for the law's supporters, one for its critics, and a neutral editor checks the rules. The editor also asks of each sentence: would we write it the same way about the other side?
Both side reviewers give at least 4 of 5, and no serious problem
We hid 13 errors in a copy of the page, such as a wrong date, a misquote and one group's figure shown as everyone's. The fact-checker had to find them without knowing they were there.

sections.title: What each round found
paras: No fact-check found a claim that its sources didn't support, only sentences that said more than the sources did. The fairness panel failed twice before both side reviewers gave the page 4 of 5.

sections.title: What's still open
paras: These suggestions change a card, a label or the balance between sides, so they wait for the next full round. Some contradict each other; we list both views rather than pick one quietly.
items: Card 5's evidence label should use the same "with limits" wording as card 1, because both rest on the same Florida study.
Reviewers disagree on whether to quote Sen. Harrell in full in Option A, and on what card 4's label should say about emergency safety.
Option B's list of costs is longer than its list of benefits; reviewers suggested ways to even them out without changing the evidence.
Officials answer the one named critic on several cards, because our sources quote few critics. The next trials will look harder for more voices.
Several lines can be plainer, and the argument cards could say when and where each person spoke.

sections.title: What this can't do
paras: All the checkers are AI, like the writer, so they may share blind spots. Hiding test errors measures only the kinds of errors we thought to hide.
The checkers compare this page with the sources we saved. They can't tell what is missing from those sources.
The two side reviewers stand in for real people's views. They are not real people.

sections.title: See every report
paras: Every check, report and fix is public in the project's repository, in trials/001-hb1009-high-school-cellphones/verification.md.
